significance.quote: The observed excess of events over the expected background has a significance of 8.2 standard deviations.

summary.plain: ATLAS observed two photons (particles of light) scattering off each other, using the strong electromagnetic fields of lead nuclei that pass close to one another without touching; those fields act as a beam of nearly real photons.
summary.technical: Ultraperipheral Pb+Pb collisions at 5.02 TeV per nucleon pair, 1.73 nb⁻¹ (Nov 2018): 59 γγ → γγ candidates against a background of 12 ± 3 events, 8.2σ significance, fiducial cross section 78 ± 13 (stat.) ± 7 (syst.) ± 3 (lumi.) nb.

title: Observation of light-by-light scattering in ultraperipheral Pb+Pb collisions with the ATLAS detector
why_it_matters: Light-by-light scattering is forbidden in the classical theory of electrodynamics; in the Standard Model it proceeds at one-loop level via virtual box diagrams involving electrically charged fermions or W bosons. The paper notes that extensions of the Standard Model (for example magnetic monopoles, vector-like fermions and axion-like particles) can add contributions, so the measurement is sensitive to new physics.
